response.original_title: Saint Germain: The Count Who Never Died
response.overview: In 1743, a man walked into the court of Louis XV with no past, no origin, and no name anyone could verify. He called himself the Comte de Saint-Germain. He spoke a dozen languages without an accent, remembered dead kings as personal acquaintances, and across thirty years at the highest courts in Europe — never aged.  A century later, his name crossed an ocean, and an American mining engineer drank from a golden cup on the slopes of Mount Shasta and built a religion around the encounter. When the federal government tried to prosecute it, the case climbed to the Supreme Court.
